content: Hi, I am a new contributor. I would like to pick up bisection for continuous f : ℝ → ℝ from here. Should the first version target ℝ or should I generalize? Where should the definitions live? Is anyone interested in advising (answering my potentially dumb or silly questions) or reviewing it?

I think having a version for R\mathbb{R}R is quite all right. Just maybe generalize to functions from some interval as opposed to the whole real line. If you are new to lean, I would worry first about getting something to work as opposed to maximal generality (and in this instance the more general versions are also different in other ways anyway, at least the ones I know). For potentially dumb or silly questions, you are more than welcome to ask in #new members (in fact maybe the thread should be moved there), it's what it's meant for. Feel free to ping me for reviews.
@Luigi Massacci Would you mind taking a look? https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/42916
I can take a look in the weekend
and an aside, you can reference pull requests to mathlib directly in zulip, there is a linkifier for it. Eg this works: #42916

@Luigi Massacci I wrote more in a PR comment, but, personally I wanted the convergence theory and an API. Everything else was speculation about what other people might want or what I might want in the future.

I'll take part of the blame: I think my suggestion to maybe write it in interval form was thoughtless. I would drop all of that. Stick to R\mathbb{R}R and it will allow you to do away with 90% of the cruft that comes with it (State, etc). If you want make a new PR or just keep it on top of this one. Sorry for leading you astray
